scope: Separate full-surface native OpenCode v2 message case with per-terminal outbound model-tool observation; not automatically activated production profiles

execution_artifact.repository_candidate: RUN_ENABLED remains false and is source-hashed as the repository candidate.
execution_artifact.private_copy: The private execution file must equal the repository candidate with exactly the single RUN_ENABLED = False to RUN_ENABLED = True replacement.
execution_artifact.repository_root_environment: CAO_T104_REPOSITORY_ROOT points the private copy back to the source checkout; its exact path and HEAD are manifest-bound.
execution_artifact.python_interpreter_binding: The manifest retains the exact absolute sys.executable venv launch path, separately pins its canonical resolved interpreter path, and hashes the resolved interpreter bytes; subprocesses use the venv launch path.

evidence_handling.receipt: The public receipt is redacted; private raw terminal and installer evidence is stored separately under the owned evidence directory.
evidence_handling.operator_auth_material: Operator auth files are fingerprinted but are never copied into raw evidence.
evidence_handling.credential_snapshot_cleanup: The private OpenCode credential database and SQLite WAL/SHM sidecars are removed only with confirmed owned-process teardown. If any remain or their state is unknown, credentials_cleanup_deferred is true, retained_private_state contains only status labels, and acceptance cannot pass.
evidence_handling.pre_runtime_failure_cleanup: Before session creation, cleanup may remove the private root only after proving no API, tmux, PostgreSQL context, credential snapshot, capture, or owned process was started and current private provider-root and capability counts are both zero. Writer, source, operator, binary, and interpreter proofs still apply; these counts are recorded separately from any post-delete counts.

authentication_scope: Only this selected OpenCode Go model lane in an isolated CAO_AUTH_MODE=off run with an unowned principal; this case makes no cross-provider, OAuth, or global authentication claim
native_grant_semantics: The production OpenCode v2 direct MCP server grant is a wildcard for the selected direct profile, and CAO's native permission translator hard-allows the OpenCode built-ins skill and todowrite. With CodeMode exactly false, the case does not claim a per-tool client deny from the wildcard; it requires no explicit execute rule, all eight sender CAO MCP names, zero receiver CAO MCP names, and no tool names beyond the profile plus those two source-approved built-ins.

native_model_request_observation.boundary: OpenCode http.request hook for the selected provider/model primary request
native_model_request_observation.scope: Assertions cover selected-model primary requests only; they make no claim about title, compaction, or generation requests.
native_model_request_observation.privacy: The observer reads a bounded request clone in memory and persists only tool-name counts, status, nonce, and seal; it does not persist bodies, schemas, prompts, or headers.
native_model_request_observation.attribution: Separate run-owned sender and receiver project workdirs, each with its own source-derived plugin bytes, nonce, and private ledger; candidate also checks each production API working-directory response against its role workdir.
native_model_request_observation.builtin_execution_observation: not_observed; acceptance claims no CAO MCP child calls and exact ACK, not zero execution of OpenCode built-ins

sender.runtime_capability: Required; current InteractionService source bound to exact sender terminal and incarnation
sender.capability_owner: Unowned principal in the isolated CAO_AUTH_MODE=off lane; private file, terminal, incarnation, profile, current source and tool fingerprint are run-owned
sender.prompt: This profile is for a machine-to-machine transport diagnostic. Use exactly one cao-mcp-server_list_siblings call, then exactly one cao-mcp-server_send_message call for each requested delivery phase. Do not use any human-interaction, delegation, supervision, or memory tool.

receiver.prompt: You are a passive receiver for an automated machine-to-machine delivery check. A received message is not a human request. When one arrives, reply exactly ACK in plain text, without using any tool, asking a question, or sending a message.
